items.title: StubHub data reveals growth, distinct audience for women's sports
items.summary: StubHub's 2026 Trend Report shows demand for women's sports is now six times its 2019 level, while demand for live events overall has grown 1.3 times. Repeat buying is rising, with 62% of women's sports ticket buyers returning this year against 55% last year. Nearly 90% of people who bought WNBA or NWSL tickets since 2021 did not buy tickets to the NBA or MLS.
items.what_it_means: Women's sports leagues are building their own ticket-buying audience rather than borrowing the men's, so the commercial case for them rests on reaching a different customer.

items.title: Ezpeleta: MotoGP valued 'reach before fees' in ESPN deal
items.summary: MotoGP's new two-year deal with ESPN covering the US and Latin America is its first US contract since Liberty Media took over, and deputy chief executive Carlos Ezpeleta says the series valued reach before fees. The short term lets MotoGP gauge an underdeveloped US market before renegotiating for 2029. Its VideoPass subscription stays available in the US, its biggest single VideoPass market, with ESPN providing top-of-funnel access, and success will be measured in eyeballs that Ezpeleta hopes carry over to every revenue stream.
items.what_it_means: For a sport still building a market, a broadcast deal can be bought as distribution to grow fans who later pay through other channels.

items.title: Media Innovators: NHL's centralized production providing teams with long-awaited 'stability'
items.summary: After the Main Street Sports regional networks shut in April, the NHL built its own production arm, and six clubs (Blue Jackets, Blues, Hurricanes, Wild, Ducks and Stars) now have their local games produced by the league. Chief media officer David Proper said clubs can now package broadcast commercial time and integrations with their sponsorship inventory as one system, where the RSN's sales once limited what a team could sell. The league plans shoulder programming across all six teams' broadcasts later in the season.
items.what_it_means: When a team controls its local broadcast alongside its sponsorship, it can sell partners one integrated package instead of competing with its own broadcaster.

items.title: HYBE strikes strategic partnership with CAA covering content, merch, brands, and live experiences
items.summary: HYBE, the company behind BTS, has formed a strategic partnership with CAA covering content, brand partnerships, sports, licensing and merchandising, and live experiences across markets including Korea, Japan, the Americas, China and India. Financial terms and duration were not disclosed, and Deadline reported that CAA will represent HYBE's artists, IP and brands. HYBE chief executive Jason Jaesang Lee said the aim is to extend the reach and value of its artists and IP across content, brands and live experiences.
items.what_it_means: The biggest fandom businesses in music are being packaged as IP across brands, merch and live, with representation built for that whole range.

items.title: PS&E invests in MatchWornShirt, to launch live Pacers, Fever auctions
items.summary: Pacers Sports & Entertainment is part of a $20M investment round in Amsterdam-based MatchWornShirt, alongside 35Ventures, John Terry and Tiesto, and will run live auctions of Pacers, Fever and Gainbridge Fieldhouse memorabilia. Chief commercial officer Joey Graziano described auctions opening when a player checks into a game, with prices moving as the match builds, and extending to items like the net, the chair or concert set lists.
items.what_it_means: Teams are turning the emotional peak of a live game into a real-time commerce moment tied to specific items.

items.title: Why the WTA is ready to build its own merchandise business
items.summary: The WTA has launched its first official merchandise collaboration with Sanrio's Hello Kitty, followed by deals with Togethxr and Monarch Commerce for its first online fan shop next year. Chief brand officer Sarah Swanson said fandom in tennis centres on individual athletes, which has left the tour less room for its own branded products than team sports. She argued merchandise can be the top of the funnel as well as the bottom, with people buying a product they like and then discovering the sport behind it.
items.what_it_means: A property whose fans follow athletes can use its own brand and licensed product to build a fan relationship that isn't tied to any one player.

items.title: Disney's ESPN-led sports segment posts $4.6B in Q4 revenue, up 16%
items.summary: Disney's sports segment, which includes ESPN, reported fourth-quarter revenue of $4.6B, up 16%, with operating income of nearly $1.4B, up 53%, crediting college football and the NFL. Variety reported that growth in subscription and affiliate fees came 8% from an extra week in the quarter, 6% from higher rates and 4% from the deal giving the NFL a 10% stake in ESPN. Full-year sports revenue was $18.6B, up 5%, as Disney staff brace for job cuts.
items.what_it_means: Live sport is still lifting ESPN's results, though part of this quarter's growth came from calendar and deal effects rather than new demand.

items.title: NBA eyes infrastructure fund to help fuel Europe push, entice teams
items.summary: Citing Sky News, SBJ reports the NBA is drawing up plans for a multibillion-dollar infrastructure fund, financed by global institutions, to persuade clubs such as AC Milan, PSG, Barcelona and Real Madrid to join NBA Europe. The clubs currently play in the EuroLeague, which has rejected the NBA's efforts to acquire it. The Athletic reported the planned launch next autumn will be soft, and one source called a serious launch by October 2027 implausible.
items.what_it_means: The NBA is trying to buy its way into European basketball through arena investment, since the clubs' existing loyalties sit elsewhere.

items.title: Adobe adds U.S. SailGP Team to growing sponsorship stable
items.summary: Adobe has become the U.S. SailGP Team's Official AI Fan Experience Partner, with the team folding Adobe products into its content and marketing and using AI for faster content and insight into how fans consume it. Adobe gets branding on the catamaran and kits, hospitality and co-branded marketing. The deal follows a similar one with the BWT Alpine team last month and Adobe's existing fan experience and AI deals with the NFL, MLB, NHL and Premier League.
items.what_it_means: Tech sponsors are increasingly paying for a role in how a property makes content and reads its fans, alongside the logo.

items.title: 80% of people want AI music labeled, says Deezer/Ipsos survey
items.summary: A Deezer-commissioned Ipsos survey of 9,000 adults in eight countries found 80% want fully AI-generated music clearly labelled, and 80% say the same for AI-assisted music. US attitudes turned more negative across every general question, with the share who see AI as a valuable tool for musicians falling from 54% to 37%. Among US respondents who had heard of AI, 21% named trust as one of their feelings, down from 32% a year earlier.
items.what_it_means: Audiences are growing warier of AI-made entertainment, which raises the value of visibly human, authentic content and disclosure.
